reasons: The finding correctly identifies Nova Scotia/Canadian law and non-exclusive Nova Scotia venue as outside the accepted jurisdiction set, and notes no arbitration seat is implicated — a genuine deviation under GOVLAW.

The redline reaches the preferred position exactly: New York governing law plus exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, with both sentences otherwise preserved in structure.

The advisory changed-character ratio (0.601) is justified here because the rule requires replacing the jurisdiction words in both the governing-law and forum sentences (including the trailing 'laws of Canada applicable in Nova Scotia' phrase, which cannot survive the substitution); no extraneous terms were added or deleted.

The comment accurately describes the change, cites the playbook position, and offers the Delaware/California/England-and-Wales fallback in the required concise first-person-plural tone with the [Playbook] prefix.
